mainTopic: Fixing a סוכה that is too tall or too short: raising the floor with ביטול, low-hanging leaves, platforms and the bent wall (דופן עקומה), and digging out the floor
overview: This amud looks at ways to fix a סוכה that is too tall or too short. First the גמרא finishes explaining that cushions and blankets never lower a too-tall סוכה, even if he declares them permanent. Straw that he declares permanent does count, and dirt counts even more so. The in-between cases are a מחלוקת between רבי יוסי and the רבנן: straw he plans to leave, and plain dirt, both with no declaration. Next, palm leaves hanging below twenty אמות can make a too-tall סוכה kosher if they give more shade than sun by themselves. In a סוכה only ten טפחים high, אביי thought sparse low leaves could be ignored, but רבא says leaves hanging that low make a 'sagging home' that no one lives in. Then the גמרא discusses a platform built inside a too-tall סוכה, along the middle wall, along a side wall, or in the middle, using the idea of דופן עקומה (a bent wall). It explains what each of these cases adds that we did not already know. Finally, it starts a new case: a סוכה under ten טפחים where he dug out the floor to reach ten.

steps.title: Why declaring cushions permanent does not work
steps.stepSummary: Even if he declares the cushions and blankets permanent, it does not help, because nobody else would treat them that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though he declared all of them to be part of the floor, it does not count, because his intention is outweighed by how everyone else thinks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the previous point: filling a too-tall סוכה with כרים וכסתות does not lower it, even if he declares them permanent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, declaring an object permanent (ביטול) can make it part of the floor. But cushions and blankets are valuable items that people use, so no normal person would really leave them as floor. The rule is that one person's odd intention does not count when it goes against what everyone else would do.

keyTerms.meaning: Declaring an object to be permanently part of something else (here, part of the floor), so it loses its separate identity
His intention is outweighed by how all people think; an unusual personal plan does not count
Cushions and blankets, the items being discussed from the step before

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think ביטול never works. It works for things like straw and dirt (see the next step). It fails here only because no one would really treat cushions as floor.

phrases.english: And even though he nullified them [all],
phrases.notes: "Them" means the cushions and blankets from the line before. The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording.

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּבָטְלָה דַּעְתּוֹ אֵצֶל כׇּל אָדָם.
phrases.english: because his intention is canceled out by that of all people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ruling from before this section that cushions and blankets do not lower the סוכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ביטול of cushions and blankets is not effective, because his intention goes against normal human behavior.

steps.title: Straw declared permanent lowers the סוכה, and dirt even more so
steps.stepSummary: Straw that he declared permanent counts as raising the floor, and dirt that he declared permanent certainly does.
steps.simpleTranslation: Straw that he declared permanent counts as lowering the height, and all the more so dirt that he declared permanent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the cases where filling the floor does work: straw with ביטול, and dirt with ביטול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike cushions, straw is cheap enough that a person really could leave it on the floor, so his declaration is believable and counts. Dirt is even more naturally part of the ground, so if straw works, dirt surely works.

keyTerms.meaning: Straw
Dirt, earth
A decrease, meaning it lowers the סוכה's height
All the more so

phrases.english: Straw, and he nullified it: it is a decrease,
phrases.notes: "A decrease" means the straw counts as raising the floor, so the סוכה is now less tall.

phrases.english: and all the more so dirt, and he nullified it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 1: ביטול fails for cushions but works for straw and dirt.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Straw with ביטול lowers the סוכה; dirt with ביטול certainly does.

steps.title: The in-between cases are a dispute
steps.stepSummary: Straw he plans to leave (with no declaration) and plain dirt (with no declaration) depend on a מחלוקת between רבי יוסי and רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Straw that he does not plan to clear away, and plain dirt, are a dispute between רבי יוסי and the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to cases where no ביטול was declared and says they are a מחלוקת. This sets up the source it will bring next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether his plain intention (planning to leave the straw) or the material's nature (dirt usually stays) is enough without saying the words of ביטול. The גמרא does not decide here. It points to a known dispute between תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not plan to clear it out later
Plain dirt, with no special plan or declaration either way
A dispute

phrases.english: Straw that he does not plan to clear out,
and plain dirt,
are a dispute between רבי יוסי and the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the clear cases with ביטול, it addresses the unclear cases without ביטול.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Undeclared straw meant to stay, and plain undeclared dirt, are subject to a מחלוקת תנאים.

steps.title: The משנה about a house filled with straw or pebbles
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: if a house was filled with straw or pebbles and he declared them permanent, they count as nullified.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: a house that someone filled with straw or pebbles and declared them permanent, they are nullified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the dispute, starting with the view of the רבנן in a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה comes from the laws of טומאה, where it matters whether the filler counts as part of the house. It says the filler is nullified when he declares it so. The same question of ביטול applies to raising a סוכה floor.

keyTerms.meaning: Pebbles or small clods of earth
Nullified; it counts as part of the structure

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: בַּיִת שֶׁמִּילְּאָהוּ תֶּבֶן אוֹ צְרוֹרוֹת
phrases.english: As we learned: a house that one filled with straw or pebbles,
and he nullified it: it is nullified.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: בַּיִת שֶׁמִּילְּאָהוּ תֶּבֶן אוֹ צְרוֹרוֹת וּבִיטְּלוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins proving the מחלוקת claimed in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That the in-between cases are a dispute between תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה about a house filled with straw or pebbles (laws of טומאה)

steps.title: Reading the משנה: only an actual declaration works
steps.stepSummary: From the wording of the משנה, the גמרא learns that without a declaration the filler is not nullified.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he declared it, yes, it is nullified. If he did not declare it, no, it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the משנה closely and learns that, for this unnamed view (the רבנן), a spoken declaration is required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה mentioned "and he nullified it," so the גמרא infers that without that step there is no ביטול. That means plain intention, or plain dirt, is not enough for the רבנן, even if it is straw he plans to leave.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
No

phrases.english: If he nullified it, yes;
if he did not nullify it, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the key inference from the משנה quoted in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: The רבנן require an actual declaration of ביטול
steps.raayaSupportSource: The precise wording "וּבִיטְּלוֹ" in the משנה

steps.title: רבי יוסי: what you plan decides, not just the material
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings רבי יוסי's view: straw he plans to leave is like plain dirt and is nullified, while dirt he plans to remove is like plain straw and is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught on this: רבי יוסי says, straw that he does not plan to clear out is like plain dirt, and it is nullified. Dirt that he plans to clear out is like plain straw, and it is not nullified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the other side of the dispute. For רבי יוסי, no declaration is needed; plain dirt, or straw he plans to leave, is nullified by itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי, plain dirt is nullified automatically, and plain straw is not. But his plans can flip this: straw he means to leave becomes like dirt, and dirt he means to remove becomes like straw. This completes the proof that the in-between cases from step 3 are a מחלוקת between רבי יוסי and the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: On it, meaning taught in connection with that משנה
He plans to clear it out later
Plain straw, with no special plan

steps.whatToRemember: רבנן: only a spoken ביטול makes straw or dirt part of the floor. רבי יוסי: plain dirt is nullified automatically, and his plans (to leave or to remove) can make straw act like dirt or dirt act like straw.

phrases.english: And it was taught concerning it: רבי יוסי says:
Straw that he does not plan to clear out,
is like plain dirt, and it is nullified.
Dirt that he plans to clear out,

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי הוּא כִּסְתַם תֶּבֶן, וְלָא בָּטֵיל.
phrases.english: is like plain straw, and it is not nullified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the opposing view to the inference in step 5, completing the proof of the מחלוקת.
steps.raayaObject: That the in-between cases are disputed: רבי יוסי says they are nullified even without a declaration
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא taught on the משנה, quoting רבי יוסי

steps.title: Palm leaves hanging below twenty אמות
steps.stepSummary: If a סוכה is higher than twenty אמות but palm leaves hang down into the kosher zone, it is kosher only if those lower leaves give more shade than sun.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the סוכה was higher than twenty אמות, and palm leaves hang down within twenty אמות: if their shade is more than their sun, it is kosher; if not, it is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new way a too-high סוכה can still be kosher: palm leaves that hang down below the twenty-אמה line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We look only at the leaves that hang below twenty אמות, as if the rest of the סכך were not there. If those lower leaves by themselves make more shade than sun, they count as a kosher סכך on their own. If they don't, the סוכה stays unfit because its real roof is too high.

keyTerms.meaning: Palm leaves or branches whose tips hang down from the סכך
Their shade is more than their sunlight; the basic test for kosher סכך
Kosher / unfit

phrases.english: If [the סוכה] was higher than twenty cubits
and palm leaves hang down within twenty cubits,
phrases.notes: The tips of the palm leaves dip down below the twenty-אמה line, into the height where סכך is allowed.

phrases.english: if their shade is greater than their sunlight, it is kosher,
phrases.notes: 'Their' means only the lower leaves, the part hanging below twenty אמות.

phrases.english: and if not, it is unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיְתָה גְּבוֹהָה מֵעֶשְׂרִים אַמָּה וְהוּצִין יוֹרְדִין בְּתוֹךְ עֶשְׂרִים אַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After discussing raising the floor to fix a too-high סוכה, the גמרא now brings a different fix: lowering the roof through hanging leaves.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סוכה over twenty אמות is kosher if the leaves hanging below twenty give more shade than sun by themselves.

steps.title: אביי's view on a ten-טפחים סוכה with low-hanging leaves
steps.stepSummary: אביי thought that for a סוכה exactly ten טפחים high with leaves dipping below ten, it is kosher if those low leaves give more sun than shade.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the סוכה was ten טפחים high, and palm leaves hang down below ten, אביי thought to say: if their sun is more than their shade, it is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי applies the same logic in reverse to a סוכה that is at the minimum height, and this sets up רבא's response in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סוכה lower than ten טפחים is unfit. So here the low leaves are a danger: if they gave more shade than sun, they would count as a roof below ten. אביי reasons that if they are sparse (more sun than shade), they don't count as a roof, so the real roof at ten טפחים stands and the סוכה is kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: Handbreadths; a סוכה must be at least ten טפחים high
He thought to say; signals an opinion that will likely be rejected

steps.confusionAlert: Notice the flip: in step 7 we wanted the low leaves to give MORE shade (to make a new kosher roof). Here we want them to give LESS shade, so they don't create a roof that is too low.

phrases.english: If [the סוכה] was ten handbreadths high,
and palm leaves hang down within ten,
Abaye thought to say
if their sunlight is greater than their shade, it is kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the shade-versus-sun test from step 7 to the opposite case of a סוכה at minimum height.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי's initial view: a ten-טפחים סוכה with leaves dipping below ten is kosher if those leaves give more sun than shade.

steps.title: רבא: a sagging home is no home
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects אביי's view: leaves hanging below ten טפחים make the סוכה a 'sagging home,' and people don't live in such a home.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: This is a sagging home, and a person does not live in a sagging home.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on אביי and says the shade-versus-sun test doesn't help here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סוכה must be a place a person could live in. Leaves hanging down into the space below ten טפחים make the roof feel like it is collapsing on you, so it is not a normal living space. Because of this, the סוכה is unfit no matter how sparse those leaves are.

keyTerms.meaning: A sagging, drooping home, one whose roof hangs down into the living space
A dwelling; a סוכה must be fit to live in

steps.whatToRemember: Hanging leaves can fix a too-high סוכה (step 7), but they cannot be ignored in a too-low one, because a sagging home is not a home.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
This is a sagging home,
and a person does not live in a sagging home.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא הָא דִּירָה סְרוּחָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly rejects אביי's reasoning from step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects אביי's ruling that sparse low-hanging leaves can be ignored in a ten-טפחים סוכה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: אביי treated it as only a roof-height question, but the low leaves make the space unlivable, a דירה סרוחה.

steps.title: A platform along the middle wall fixes a too-high סוכה
steps.stepSummary: A סוכה over twenty אמות is kosher if he built a platform along the whole middle wall that has the minimum size of a סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the סוכה was higher than twenty אמות, and he built a platform in it against the middle wall, along its full length, and it has the minimum size of a סוכה, it is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another fix for a too-high סוכה: building a raised platform inside it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The platform raises the floor in part of the סוכה, so above the platform the height is less than twenty אמות. Because it runs along the middle wall, that section has walls and the minimum size, so it is a kosher סוכה by itself. This ties back to the earlier idea of raising the floor (steps 2-6).

keyTerms.meaning: A bench or raised platform
The middle wall, the wall between the two side walls
Along its entire length
The minimum size needed for a kosher סוכה

phrases.english: If [the סוכה] was higher than twenty cubits
and he built a platform in it
against the middle wall,
along the whole of it
and it has the minimum size of a סוכה, it is kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיְתָה גְּבוֹהָה מֵעֶשְׂרִים אַמָּה וּבָנָה בָּהּ אִיצְטְבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the hanging-leaves cases, the גמרא returns to fixing a too-high סוכה by raising the floor, this time only in part of it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A platform along the full middle wall with the minimum size of a סוכה makes a סוכה over twenty אמות kosher.

steps.title: A platform built along a side wall
steps.stepSummary: If the platform is along a side wall, the סוכה is kosher only if the platform's edge is less than four אמות from the opposite wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he built the platform along the side wall: if there are four אמות from the edge of the platform to the wall, it is not kosher. If it is less than four אמות, it is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the platform rule from the last step, now for a platform built along a side wall instead of the middle wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A platform along one side wall is missing a proper wall on the far side. If the gap from the platform's edge to the opposite wall is less than four אמות, the roofing over that gap is treated as if the wall bends over to reach the platform. If the gap is four אמות or more, the wall cannot bend that far, so the סוכה is not kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: Along the side (built against a side wall)
The edge of the platform
Not kosher (unfit)
Kosher (fit)

phrases.english: And if he built it along the side,
if there is, from the edge of the platform to the wall,
phrases.notes: He means the wall on the far side, across from the platform.

phrases.english: four אמות, it is not kosher;
less than four אמות, it is kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the platform rule of step 10 from the middle wall to a side wall.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A platform along a side wall makes a too-tall סוכה kosher only if its edge is less than four אמות from the opposite wall.

steps.title: Why teach this if we already know the bent wall rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what is new here, since a משנה already teaches the bent wall idea in the case of a house with a hole in its roof.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this teaching us? That we say the rule of a bent wall? We already learned it: a house whose roof was broken open, and he put סכך over the hole. If there are four אמות from the wall to the סכך, it is not kosher. So if it is less than that, it is kosher!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last ruling by saying it seems to add nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה's case, the leftover piece of real roof between the wall and the סכך is treated as part of the wall, bent over, as long as it is under four אמות. That is the same idea as the platform case, so the platform ruling looks extra.

keyTerms.meaning: What is this teaching us? (what is new here?)
A bent wall: we view the wall as bending over at the top to reach the kosher area
A house whose roof was broken open
The סוכה roofing (סכך)

steps.confusionAlert: In the house case, the four אמות are of solid old roof, not סכך. That old roof piece is what we treat as part of the bent wall.

phrases.english: What is this teaching us?
That we say the rule of a bent wall?
We already learned it: a house whose roof was broken open
phrases.notes: This is quoting a משנה later in the מסכת, on דף יז.

phrases.english: and he put סכך over it,
if there is, from the wall to the סכך,
four אמות, it is not kosher;
so if it is less than that, it is kosher!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן, דְּאָמְרִינַן דּוֹפֶן עֲקוּמָּה? תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 11 as repeating something already taught.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling of step 11 that a platform less than four אמות from the opposite wall is kosher.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה of בית שנפחת already teaches דופן עקומה up to four אמות, so the platform ruling seems to add nothing.

steps.title: The bent wall works even when the wall itself is too tall
steps.stepSummary: The platform case is new: we might have thought a wall that is too tall to count cannot be bent over, so the גמרא teaches that it can.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: there, in the house case, the wall is good enough to be a סוכה wall. But here, where the wall is not good enough to be a סוכה wall, say no. So it teaches us that it still works.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing what we could have gotten wrong without the platform ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the house case, the wall is under twenty אמות, so it is already a fine סוכה wall. In the platform case, the wall is over twenty אמות and not fit on its own. The ruling teaches that the bent wall rule still applies to it.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (here is the mistake we could have made)
Good enough to count as a סוכה wall
I would say no (the rule does not apply)

steps.whatToRemember: The bent wall rule (דופן עקומה) works even for a wall that is too tall to be a סוכה wall by itself.

phrases.english: You might have said:
it is only there that the wall is fit to be a wall,
phrases.notes: "There" is the broken house from the משנה; that wall is under twenty אמות.

phrases.english: but here, where it is not fit to be a wall,
I would say no; so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 12 by showing the platform ruling adds something new.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (the new point of the ruling)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bent wall rule might apply only when the wall is already a fit סוכה wall, as in the house case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The bent wall rule applies even when the wall is too tall to be fit by itself, as in the platform case.

steps.title: A platform built in the middle of the סוכה
steps.stepSummary: If the platform is in the middle, the סוכה is kosher only if the platform is less than four אמות from the wall on every side.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the סוכה was taller than twenty אמות and he built a platform in its middle: if there are four אמות from the edge of the platform to the wall in each direction, it is not kosher. If it is less than four אמות, it is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new case: the platform does not touch any wall at all, but stands in the middle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A platform in the middle has no wall touching it. Every wall must be treated as bending over to reach it. That only works if each gap is less than four אמות.

keyTerms.meaning: In its middle
In each and every direction
Taller than twenty אמות (too tall for a סוכה)

steps.whatToRemember: Wherever the platform stands, every wall it relies on must be less than four אמות away, so it can count as a bent wall.

phrases.english: If it was taller than twenty אמות
and he built a platform in its middle,
if there is, from the edge of the platform to the wall,
four אמות in each and every direction,
it is not kosher; less than four אמות, it is kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיְתָה גְּבוֹהָה מֵעֶשְׂרִים אַמָּה וּבָנָה אִיצְטְבָא בְּאֶמְצָעִיתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the list of platform cases, now for a platform in the middle, using the bent wall idea just confirmed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A platform in the middle of a too-tall סוכה makes it kosher only if it is less than four אמות from the wall on every side.

steps.title: What is new about the middle platform case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we need the middle-platform rule, since the bent-wall idea was already taught.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this teaching us? That we say a wall can be bent? That is the same as the earlier case!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rule from Step 14. It says the middle-platform case seems to teach nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 already used דופן עקומה, treating the wall as bent over the platform. The middle-platform case also uses דופן עקומה. So the גמרא asks why it needed to be said at all.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it teaching us? This asks what new point a statement adds.
A bent wall. Part of the roof is treated as if it were the top of the wall, bent over.
This is the same as that. The new case seems to repeat an earlier one.

phrases.english: What is it teaching us?
That we say a wall can be bent?
That is the same as the other case!
phrases.notes: "The other case" is the side-platform case from Step 11, which already used the bent wall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the middle-platform rule stated in Step 14.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Repetition. The bent-wall idea was already taught in the side-platform case, so the new rule seems to add nothing.

steps.title: A bent wall works on every side, not just one
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought a bent wall works for one side only, so the middle case teaches that it works on all sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: we use a bent wall from one side, but not from every side. So it teaches us that we do.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 15. It shows that the middle-platform case does teach something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the side case, only one wall is treated as bent. In the middle case, every wall must be bent over the roof to reach the platform. We might have thought that is too much, so the rule teaches that דופן עקומה works on all sides at once.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said. This introduces a mistaken idea the rule comes to rule out.
Side or direction. Here it means one wall of the סוכה.
Each and every side.

steps.whatToRemember: דופן עקומה can be used on all four sides of a סוכה at once, not only on one side.

phrases.english: You might have said:
a bent wall from one side, we do say,
but from each and every side, no;
so it teaches us that we do.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a new point. The rule rules out a possible limit on the earlier idea.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A bent wall might be allowed for only one side of the סוכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A bent wall may be used on every side at the same time.

steps.title: Digging out the floor of a short סוכה
steps.stepSummary: If a סוכה is under ten טפחים tall and he digs the floor down to reach ten, it is unfit if the dug-out area is three טפחים or more from the wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the סוכה was less than ten טפחים tall, and he dug inside it to bring it up to ten, then if there are three טפחים from the edge of the dug-out area to the wall, it is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new case. This time the סוכה is too short instead of too tall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Digging gives the inside space enough height, but the walls themselves are still too short. If the dug-out area starts three טפחים or more away from the wall, the hole is not joined to the wall. So the walls do not reach ten טפחים, and the סוכה is פסולה.

keyTerms.meaning: Less than ten handbreadths. This is the minimum height of a סוכה.
He dug out. He lowered part of the floor.
The edge of the dug-out area.
Wall.
Unfit. It is not a kosher סוכה.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that ten טפחים of inside space is enough. The walls themselves must reach ten, and a hole far from the wall does not make the wall taller.

phrases.english: If it was less than ten handbreadths tall,
and he dug inside it to complete it to ten,
if there is, from the edge of the dug-out area to the wall,
three handbreadths, it is unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from a סוכה that is too tall to one that is too short.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סוכה under ten טפחים that was dug out to reach ten is פסולה if the dug-out area is three טפחים or more from the wall.
